plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, umbrella-shaped tree that lights up the tropical summer with fiery clusters of scarlet-orange blossoms. Each flower has a standout petal streaked with cream and gold, set against feathery, fern-like leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring through summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak flowering from November to February in Madagascar and similar regions
plants.location: Madagascar, where it is native, and the tropical Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: The Royal Poinciana is endangered in its native Madagascar, yet it is planted in warm regions all over the world. Its long, woody seed pods rattle in the wind when they dry.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: A graceful evergreen shrub that flowers when most of the garden has gone quiet. Its delicate, lightly fragrant blooms open in drifts of white, pink and rose, and their golden stamens attract winter pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to mid-winter, from about October through January
plants.location: Southern Japan, and gardens in the southeastern United States and the Mediterranean
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Oil pressed from its seeds has long been used in Japan for cooking and hair care.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: A bold wildflower of the Australian bush. Its flower head is a crimson dome of tightly packed blooms ringed by deep red bracts, and it looks like a torch held up on a tall stem.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring to early summer, mainly September to November, with some flowers lingering later in cooler spots
plants.location: Sandstone ridges and forests near Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
plants.funFact: The waratah is the floral emblem of New South Wales. Its nectar-rich flower heads attract honeyeater birds, which pollinate the plant as they feed.
